requirements.statement: Package managers must be able to award a supplier package to one supplier.
requirements.source_quote: Package managers must be able to award a supplier package to one supplier.
ambiguity_notes: Which package managers may award (all, or only those responsible for the package) is not stated.
Whether an award can be undone or changed is not stated.
Where the candidate suppliers come from (bids, invited list, any supplier) is not stated.
Whether the award needs a confirmation step is not stated.
Which users the read-only state applies to (package managers, suppliers, administrators) is not stated.
Which parts of the package are locked (all fields, or only some) is not stated.
Whether anyone can unlock or edit an awarded package is not stated.

requirements.statement: Suppliers must be notified when they win.
requirements.source_quote: Suppliers must be notified when they win.
ambiguity_notes: The notification channel (email, in-app, other) is not stated.
The notification content is not stated.
Whether suppliers who do not win are notified is not stated.
Whether notification is immediate on award or can be delayed or retried is not stated.

clarifying_questions.question: Which package managers are allowed to award a package: any package manager, or only the one responsible for that package?
clarifying_questions.why_it_matters: Defines permissions for an action with commercial effect.
clarifying_questions.consequence_if_unanswered: The permission rule for awarding cannot be specified.

clarifying_questions.question: Can an award be withdrawn or changed to a different supplier after it is made, and by whom?
clarifying_questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether awarding is irreversible and whether read-only can ever be lifted.
clarifying_questions.consequence_if_unanswered: Cannot specify award reversal, error correction, or the unlock behaviour of awarded packages.

clarifying_questions.question: For whom is an awarded package read-only, and which parts of it are locked?
clarifying_questions.why_it_matters: Sets the scope of the restriction and the affected roles and data.
clarifying_questions.consequence_if_unanswered: The read-only behaviour cannot be specified beyond a general statement.

clarifying_questions.question: How should the winning supplier be notified (email, in-app, other), what should the message contain, and should unsuccessful suppliers be told too?
clarifying_questions.why_it_matters: Determines notification channel, content and recipient set.

proposed_status_changes.reason: Who the read-only state applies to, what is locked, and whether it can be lifted is not stated.
Notification channel, content and recipients beyond the winner are not stated.
